title: SocioBench: Modeling Human Behavior in Sociological Surveys with Large Language Models
findings: The study found that LLMs' accuracy in simulating human responses on religious topics showed highly significant differences across continents (p < .001). Specifically, models exhibited generally lower accuracy when simulating the personas of African respondents compared to those from Europe, North America, and Oceania. Overall accuracy for the Religion domain was among the highest of the 10 domains tested, with top-performing models achieving around 39-41% accuracy.
references: Gati V Aher, Rosa I Arriaga, and Adam Tauman Kalai. 2023. Using large language models to simulate multiple humans and replicate human subject studies. In International Conference on Machine Learning, pages 337–371. PMLR.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the accuracy of Large Language Models in simulating individual human responses to sociological survey questions about religion. The LLMs are given a demographic profile, including religious affiliation, and are evaluated on how well their chosen survey answers match the real answers of the person with that profile.
